extracted.intended_audience: general newspaper readers interested in national politics, military affairs, and current events
extracted.subtask_description: Writing or editing a newspaper news story about national political and military events, including dateline, sourcing, background, and human-interest details. Focus is on timely reporting of official actions, reactions, and context for a broad public audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dateline and byline
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a clear dateline and byline (e.g., 'Washington, Oct. 28 (P)—' and 'WRITTEN BY HARRY LEVER, STAR REPORTER').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place the location and date at the top of the story and include the reporter's name and affiliation so readers know where and by whom the dispatch was filed. This page uses multiple datelines for different items (Washington, New York, Knoxville, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Accurate quotation and prompt correction of misquotes
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure quotes are reported accurately and correct the record when a source is misquoted (example: Commander McCain 'misquoted' on atom bomb remark; a correction/clarification is included).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attribute direct quotes precisely; if an error occurs, acknowledge or publish a correction or the subject's denial, as this article does when a misquote is admitted ('I must concede I misquoted him.').

rubrics_metrics.name: Named-source attribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Attribute statements to named individuals with titles or roles (e.g., 'An aide, Capt. Walter Karig, said', 'Sen. Knowland, Rep., Cal., called', 'Rep. Edith Nourse Rogers, Rep., Mass., said').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always give the speaker's name and identifying information (rank, office, party, state, title) so readers can assess the authority and perspective of the statement; avoid unattributed or anonymous claims unless necessary and clearly labeled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide factual background and context
rubrics_metrics.description: Supply relevant background facts that explain the significance of events (e.g., Denfeld's 40‑year naval career, base pay and allowances, prior testimony before the House committee).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include biographical, financial, procedural, and historical context to help readers understand implications — salaries, positions held, prior testimony, dates of announcements, and past events that led to the current story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance by presenting multiple perspectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Include reactions from critics, supporters, official spokesmen and the subject himself (e.g., lawmakers demanding resignations, aides urging retention, Denfeld's own statements, Secretary Johnson's reply to Bates).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give voice to competing viewpoints and official responses so coverage is balanced: opposing lawmakers, administration spokesmen, personal allies, and the principal's own remarks are all represented in this article.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human-interest/detailing to humanize the subject
rubrics_metrics.description: Intersperse humanizing anecdotes and specifics (e.g., telegraph boy ringing the bell, telephone calls from friends, serenade by Fleet Reserve Association) to convey personal reaction and atmosphere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use concrete, sensory details and short anecdotes to make high-level political/military stories relatable and vivid for readers while keeping such elements factual and relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report official and procedural actions precisely
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe formal moves and procedures clearly (e.g., offers of transfer, resignations, memos, committee hearings, Senate confirmation, legislative actions and exemptions affecting projects).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reporting government actions, cite the specific action, who took it, any stated reason, and any procedural next steps (committees, floor action, legal exemptions) so readers see the mechanics and implications of official decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Credit wire services and other sources of copy
rubrics_metrics.description: Mark and credit Associated Press or other wire dispatches and indicate when material is drawn from other outlets (the page contains multiple AP datelines and references to 'Associated Press dispatches').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly attribute wire-service copy and third-party reporting; label syndicated or reprinted material and maintain editorial clarity about source and origin of each item.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use concise headlines and subheads to summarize
rubrics_metrics.description: Employ short, informative headlines and subheads (examples: 'Lawmakers Upset Over Denfeld Shift', 'Admiral Offered', 'Deluged by expressions of sympathy over his removal').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write headlines and subheads that capture the main point or hook of each item so readers can scan the page quickly; ensure they accurately reflect the story content without exaggeration.
